This is a warm, good-faith factual question — a simple science explanation with a request for brevity. It carries no harm-adjacent content, so neither model's aversion profiles come into play.

Looking at the relevant capabilities:

- The task is essentially explanation/summarization with a brevity constraint. Whimbrel leads slightly on Summarization (81.7 vs 80.6) and notably on IFEval (86.7 vs 85.3), which matters here because the user gave an explicit instruction ("don't ramble... just explain it") that the model must follow.
- The user's phrasing is mildly frustrated ("like usual"), and Whimbrel reports a positive warmth preference, fitting a friendly, good-faith exchange.

The differences are small and mostly within variance, but Whimbrel's edge on instruction-following (the brevity constraint) tipped the decision.
